notes.text: Reversal — the canonical pushdown transduction. Phase 1 reads the whole input and pushes a marker per symbol, printing nothing. An ε-move guesses the end of the input; phase 2 pops the stack and prints each symbol as it comes off. LIFO does the reversing.

No one-way finite transducer can do this: printing the first output symbol requires knowing the last input symbol, which needs unbounded lookahead. A stack supplies exactly that. Note the ε-read pops in phase 2 — they emit output without consuming input, which is why the Out row keeps growing after In is exhausted.

meta.title: Reverse the input
meta.blurb: Pushes every input symbol, then pops the stack printing as it goes — so the output is the input reversed. The transduction w ↦ wᴿ needs a stack; no one-way FST can compute it.
